speaker: Leonard
text: So, Dennis, how long have you been in America? No kidding. You speak English really well.

speaker: Dennis Kim
text: A year and a half. So do you. Except for your tendency to end sentences with prepositions.

speaker: Leonard
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Dennis Kim
text: That.

speaker: Dennis Kim
text: Is this part of the tour?

speaker: Leonard
text: Come on, Sheldon, we've hardly shown him anything.

speaker: Sheldon
text: He's not wrong. Alright. And this is my office. Oh, right. This is my, desk. These are my books. This is my door. Please close it behind you.

speaker: Dennis Kim
text: Looks like you're doing work in quantum loop corrections.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Keen observation.

speaker: Dennis Kim
text: You see where I went wrong, don't you?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Leonard? Get him out.

speaker: Leonard
text: Yeah?

speaker: Leonard
text: Come on, Dennis. I'll show you the rec center. They've got Nautilus equipment.

speaker: Dennis Kim
text: Do I look like I lift weights?

speaker: Leonard
text: Not heavy ones.

speaker: Dennis Kim
text: It's startling to me you haven't considered a Lorentz invariant or field theory approach.

speaker: Sheldon
text: You think I haven't considered it? You really think I haven't considered it?

speaker: Dennis Kim
text: Have you considered it?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Get him out, Leonard.

speaker: Leonard
text: Come on, Dennis. I'll show you the radiation lab.

speaker: Dennis Kim
text: Wow. You won the Stevenson Award?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Yes. In fact, I am the youngest person ever to win it.

speaker: Dennis Kim
text: Really? How?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Fourteen and a half.

speaker: Dennis Kim
text: You were the youngest person ever to win it?
